MODULE 01
CHARACTER FIRST
Decide who your audience will follow before you make a single image.
CREATE THE CHARACTER. DIRECT THE SCENE. BUILD THE WORLD.
Why this comes first
AI can make a beautiful face in seconds. But a face with no story is still just a picture.
A strong character has a real role and a clear identity. They have a starting point, one wall (one big problem), and something they want.
That is what makes people watch the next episode.

lines: Build the character with 8 choices
1. ROLE
Who is this person in the story? A creator, founder, artist, customer, parent, partner, employee, traveler, realtor, musician or fictional lead?
2. AUDIENCE
Who should see themselves, their wants or their world in this character?
3. STARTING POINT
Where is their life before the story starts? Think feelings, friends and work.
4. ONE WALL
Pick one clear problem. One wall keeps the story focused. Five walls confuse people.
5. DESIRE
What do they really want behind that wall? Confidence, attention, belonging, freedom, love, status, safety, clarity or a new beginning?
6. PERSONALITY
How do they talk, move, react, dress and handle stress?
7. VISUAL IDENTITY
Age range, ethnicity, skin tone, face details, hair, grooming, body type, tattoos, piercings, go-to accessories and clothing style.
8. WORLD
Where do they fit best? Buckhead, a resort, a studio, an office, a tour bus, a salon, a family home, a campus or nightlife?
Body type is part of the identity plan
Body type is not a beauty score. It is a rule that keeps your character looking the same.
Pick words that truly describe the character. Use the same words in the MASTER and the full-body DNA sheet.

lines: MODULE 05
THE CONTINUITY SYSTEM
Make every new clip feel like the next second of the same world.
CREATE THE CHARACTER. DIRECT THE SCENE. BUILD THE WORLD.
Continuity is what creates a series

The same face is not enough. Viewers notice small breaks. The hair changes, a bottle moves, the sun jumps, the crowd repeats, or the camera jumps around. Continuity locks the whole world, not just the face.

No face drift. No identity drift. No skin-tone change. No body change. No age change. No hairstyle

Product lock
Use the exact [PRODUCT] from Reference [#]. Preserve shape, size, proportions, material, color, cap,
logo, label orientation, liquid level and placement. The product never morphs, duplicates, floats or

Dialogue timing
Keep dialogue short enough for [SECONDS]. Use natural pauses, eye contact, listening and reaction

Background crowd
[COUNT] adults naturally spread throughout [LOCATION]. Each person has a different outfit, face and
activity. Nobody stares at the camera unless directed. No cloned guests or frozen crowd.
Authentic phone footage

realistic motion blur, no commercial crane movement and no impossible depth of field.

lines: Five viral patterns you can run in any niche
1. The Mystery Gift
Hook: something arrives for your character from an unknown sender.
References: identity, outfit, location, continuity, the item itself.
Why people watch: viewers need to know who sent it and demand the reveal.
Next episode: the sender stays hidden one more time, then gets revealed.
2. The Dream Location
Hook: phone-style footage that feels real inside a dream spot.
References: identity, outfit, location exterior and interior, one product.
Why people watch: continuity makes made-up events feel like a real series.
Next episode: one new event, same world, same character.
3. The Shopping Spree
Hook: your character came to browse and leaves with everything.
References: identity, exact outfit, store environment, bags and product.
Why people watch: locals recognize the place, and brands may repost it.
Next episode: fitting room, checkout moment or outfit reveal.
4. The Night Out
Hook: nightlife chaos your audience understands at a glance.
References: characters, outfits, venue, signage, table service.
Why people watch: a bold location, matching sound and comment-section debate.
Next episode: the morning after, or the behind-the-scenes reaction.
5. The Nervous First Client
Hook: a first-timer walks into your world of work.
References: your identity, work outfit, real workspace, your tools.
Why people watch: emotion plus expert authority builds trust in your skill.
Next episode: the transformation, a lesson or the client’s reaction.
